subject: POC Enablement Matrix — BlueHarbor trial orchestration & approvals
messages:
From: Lucas Moreno <lucas.moreno@blueharbor.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@blueharbor.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Initial POC requirements and next steps

Hi Rachel / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation. I promised to share our high-level POC needs so your team can propose an enablement plan and a clear RACI. Attached is a short worksheet with our functional priorities (blueharbor-poc-requirements.xlsx).

Top-level success criteria we need to validate in the trial:
- Inference quality: match baseline intent extraction on our 10k test prompts (F1 >= 0.88)
- Latency: p95 generation <= 350ms for typical 512-token requests (we can relax for very large batches)
- Cost: sustained per-1k-token cost estimate to be within 30% of your hosted benchmark for our workload profile
- Security & data handling: clear data path for logs, audit events, and retention controls (we require SOC2 evidence)
- Integration: sample app integration via API and SDK without production downtime

Timing: we are targeting a 6-week evaluation window starting mid-June with an infra/architecture touchpoint in week 0.

What we need from Redwood:
- Draft RACI mapping for infra / app / security / procurement (who at Redwood owns each lane)
- Recommended trial topology: hosted vs dedicated vs private (quick pros/cons for our environment)
- SOC2 and data-retention paperwork (or pointer to your security portal)
- Proposed kickoff date options (week of 6/14 or 6/21)

Can you share a draft enablement matrix and a short list of internal owners? Priya (cc'ed) will be our procurement lead — she needs the commercial path and any PO timing constraints.

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30m if helpful.

— Lucas
Lucas Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering | BlueHarbor AI
attachments: blueharbor-poc-requirements.xlsx

Subject: Re: Initial POC requirements and next steps

Lucas — great write-up, thanks for the worksheet. I pulled the team together and sketched an initial enablement matrix (attached: redwood-poc-enablement-matrix-v1.xlsx) that maps owners, key milestones, and the minimal artifacts we need for each lane. Key notes from our side: 

Draft owner assignments (please confirm):
- Infra & connectivity (VPC peering / on-prem options): Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwood.com) — will lead the architecture call
- Application integration (SDK calls, sample app): Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.com) — CS/solutions lead for integration playbook
- Security & compliance artefacts (SOC2, retention, audit logs): Karthik (we'll surface SOC2 report and a security runbook)
- Commercial / procurement coordination: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com) — will share trial pricing and PO path

Proposed initial timeline (high level):
1) Week 0 (kickoff): infra & security touchpoint, clarify topology (hosted/dedicated/private)
2) Week 1: integration sprint—sample app + basic eval prompts loaded
3) Weeks 2–4: tuning and metrics collection (quality + latency)
4) Week 5: business readout and decision checklist
5) Week 6: wrap + next steps (contracting/scale if successful)

Action items I am taking now:
- Drop updated enablement matrix v1 into the shared Drive (link below)
- Schedule infra architecture slot: proposed 60m on Thu 5/13 10:00–11:00 PT (Karthik, Lucas, Monica) — please confirm availability
- Ben will circulate a DocuSign proposal + pricing options for a trial slot (hosted vs dedicated)

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_blueharbor_poc
DocuSign (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/abc123

If the assignments look off to you, flag the change and we'll update the matrix.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-10T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial POC requirements and next steps — commercial / procurement notes

Priya / Lucas — looping in procurement details so we can align timelines. Two commercial paths that map to the topology Rachel mentioned: 

1) Hosted trial (fastest): short-term hosted credits with usage cap, minimal procurement paperwork, ideal if you want to evaluate quickly.
2) Dedicated trial (reserved capacity): requires an MSA addendum + short SOW, predictable throughput for load testing, better for latency-sensitive tests.

I've built a short DocuSign proposal that outlines a 6-week trial for both options and includes a one-time trial credit. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/abc123 (attached PDF: docusign-proposal-blueharbor.pdf).

Priya — if you can share your PO cadence and any legal redlines up front we can accelerate the SOW path. Typical timing: hosted trial can start within ~3–5 business days of signature; dedicated requires 2–3 weeks depending on procurement/engineering booking.

Karthik — FYI on the latency requirement Lucas listed (p95 <= 350ms). If we can get an infra topology confirmed at kickoff we can reserve test capacity for week 1.

Thanks — happy to discuss on the kickoff.

— Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel / Ben — this is helpful. Quick confirmation on owners: Karthik as infra/security owner and Monica as app integration owner works for us. Priya will handle procurement path.

A few updates on our side after internal sync:
- We absolutely need the latency SLO captured in the success criteria (p95 <= 350ms) and would like an explicit test plan for how you'll measure it (tooling, traffic profile).
- Data residency: our pilot data will be EU-resident; please call out any constraints with hosted deployments (if any) or confirm that a regional deployment is available. If regional hosting is not viable, we need a short note on the private/VPC option and what it entails (networking prerequisites).
- Network requirements doc attached: blueharbor-network-requirements.pdf — this includes IP ranges and firewall rules we use in our staging environment.

We can do the proposed Thu 5/13 10:00–11:00 PT architecture slot. Please send a calendar invite and an agenda (10m goals, 30m infra deep-dive, 20m integration next steps).
